solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The old man has got hold of a wonderful cure

indicators.note: having got hold of something means holding it, so the father's word wraps around what follows

parts.note: the old man is an affectionate name for one's father, PA
the article a, in its form before a vowel, AN
ace is slang for excellent or wonderful

explanation.surface: Dad has somehow obtained a miracle remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wonderful cure' reads as one phrase, but 'wonderful' is ACE in the wordplay and only 'cure' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy claimed to fix every ill is a cure-all, a universal remedy.

clue.text: Cops reduced — Yard's course of action

indicators.note: cut down, so the last letter of the word for cops is dropped

parts.note: cops are the police
Y is the abbreviation for yard; the 's is a link meaning has

explanation.surface: Police cutbacks: Scotland Yard's strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the London police headquarters, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or line of conduct adopted by an organisation is its chosen course of action.

clue.text: Appointing an overthrown Lib Dem leader of yesteryear

indicators.note: turned over, so the two letters of 'an' are read backwards

parts.note: Sir Menzies Campbell, Liberal Democrat leader 2006-07, was nicknamed Ming

explanation.surface: A politician recalls the appointment of a toppled former Liberal Democrat chief.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats are a UK political party.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint someone to a post is to nominate or name them for it.

clue.text: Actor seen swirling round front of cinema — bless!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the next piece
the letters of the two words before it whirl into a new order
only the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: An actor is spotted twirling outside a picture house to cheers of 'bless!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bless!' looks like an exclamation in the surface, but it is a verb defining the answer; 'seen' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To consecrate is to make holy, the same as to bless in a religious rite.

clue.text: Mountain with limited height, a first in a series

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
height cut down to its abbreviation, H

explanation.surface: A peak of modest height is the first of a range.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the first item in a sequence.

clue.text: Professional word of a particular type that conveys wisdom

definitions.text: word of a particular type that conveys wisdom

parts.note: PRO is the short form of professional
a verb is one particular class of word, a doing word

explanation.surface: An expert's choice of word passes on accumulated wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A short traditional saying that sums up practical wisdom, such as 'look before you leap'.

clue.text: New Jersey location, place for prisoners, but not women

indicators.note: the letter for women is excluded from the word before

parts.note: Princetown, a village on Dartmoor in Devon, is home to Dartmoor Prison

explanation.surface: A New Jersey jail houses men but not women.
explanation.walkthrough: Princetown is the Devon village of Dartmoor Prison; drop its W for the New Jersey university town.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in New Jersey, home of the Ivy League university of the same name.

clue.text: Dish of egg and greasy liquid served up

parts.note: an egg is round like the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: oil is a greasy liquid

explanation.surface: A dish of egg in oil is brought to the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish-style stew, and by extension any hotchpotch dish.

clue.text: The last thing you'd expect an actor to say?

definitions.text: The last thing you'd expect an actor to say?

parts.words: The last thing you'd expect an actor to say?
parts.note: not something surprising, but literally the final speech an actor delivers at the end of a play

explanation.definitionFit: A closing speech addressed to the audience when a play finishes.

clue.text: Showed some sign of life with the food being passed round

indicators.note: the food goes around the next word, as a loaf is passed round a table

parts.note: bread is basic food

explanation.surface: A patient revived as dinner was handed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word; 'being passed round' reads as a table scene but tells the food to go around the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing air in and out is the first sign that someone is alive.

clue.text: Fruit captured by capable monkey

indicators.note: the answer is held captive within the run of letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit is snatched by a clever ape.
explanation.definitionFit: A sour yellow citrus is a common example of fruit.

clue.text: Demure, needing to get with it, I have to be Methodist

parts.note: prim means modest and proper, like demure
IT on its own means fashionable, 'with it'
I have contracts to I'VE

explanation.surface: A modest person must become fashionable to join a Methodist congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing to get' and 'to be' are joining words. The Primitive Methodists were a nineteenth-century branch of Methodism.
explanation.definitionFit: A Primitive is a member of the Primitive Methodist church, so the adjective can stand for that kind of Methodist.

clue.text: Legal document for vehicle

definitions.meaning: a deed transferring ownership of property
any means of transport, such as a cart or coach

explanation.definitionFit: A deed passing property title is one sense; a means of carrying people or goods is the other.

clue.text: Word of defiance is a habit

definitions.meaning: a refusal such as 'I will not!' shortened
a customary practice; the definition includes the article

explanation.definitionFit: The contraction of 'will not' is a defiant refusal; the old noun means one's custom or usual practice.

clue.text: Cinema — cool, funny, cheap

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters of the two words are set out oddly

explanation.surface: A cool, quirky cinema with low ticket prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Economical means thrifty or inexpensive, as cheap does.

clue.text: Style of building erect hair, cut unconventionally

indicators.note: done in an unconventional way, so the letters of the three words before it are set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A punk's spiky upright hairdo, cut in an odd way, looks like a style of building.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ERECT, HAIR and CUT are rearranged by 'unconventionally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Design and style of buildings, as in Gothic or Georgian, is what the art of building is called.

clue.text: Pomposity of the male saints going round each very small home

indicators.note: the pronoun's two letters go round the following pieces

parts.note: HE is the male pronoun
very abbreviated to a small letter V
in means at home

explanation.surface: Pompous saints process round every tiny house.
explanation.walkthrough: The saints come last in the answer though the clue names them before the inner pieces; 'very small' means V written small as an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaviness, a ponderous solemnity, is a loose sense of pompousness.

clue.text: Terrible goings-on — Conservative in traditional Liberal footwear!

indicators.note: the Conservative's letter is put inside the footwear

parts.note: Liberals are stereotyped as sandal-wearers

explanation.surface: Outrage: a Tory caught wearing Liberal sandals!
explanation.walkthrough: Conservative and Liberal are UK parties; sandals are the joke footwear of the stereotyped Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandals are disgraceful events that cause public outrage.

clue.text: Mathematical value worked out by a girl, ten

indicators.note: worked out suggests the letters are rearranged to reach a result

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ten-year-old girl calculates a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: An integral is a quantity found by integration in calculus.

clue.text: What you might see in prisoners' exercise yard is compelling

parts.words: What you might see in prisoners' exercise yard
parts.note: convicts (cons) doing physical training split the answer into two words

explanation.surface: A prison exercise yard offers a gripping sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain someone is to force them, so constraining means forcing or obliging.

clue.text: Places to the north with men in a dazed state

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upward

parts.note: places means puts
OR (other ranks) are ordinary soldiers, men

explanation.surface: Men in a stupor are put up north.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a state of near-unconsciousness or bewilderment.

clue.text: Irishman leading church meeting of a spooky nature

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Irishman leads a church gathering with a ghostly air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' is a link: SEAN comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering where people try to contact the spirits of the dead.

clue.text: Through listening, recognises dissident expressions

indicators.note: the word is to be heard rather than read, so its sound gives the spelling

parts.note: to recognise something is to know it, KNOWS

explanation.surface: By listening carefully, someone picks out dissenting remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Votes or replies of 'no' are the expressions of those who disagree.

clue.text: A unit briefly installed in summer

parts.note: the short form of the unit, MM, sits in the middle of the word summer

explanation.surface: A piece of equipment is quickly fitted during the summer months.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is not built from letters: its abbreviation MM is what you see installed in suMMer, and 'briefly' says to use that short form.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousandth of a metre is a standard metric unit of length.

clue.text: Coffee time with others turning up all around

indicators.note: the reversed others are placed around time
in a down clue, up means read backwards

parts.note: et al is Latin for and others

explanation.surface: Coffee time with friends showing up all round.
explanation.walkthrough: ET AL turned up gives LATE, which goes around T.
explanation.definitionFit: A milky espresso coffee, from the Italian for milk.

clue.text: Psychiatrist's not right to quarrel

indicators.note: 'not' here means without: the psychiatrist's name is taken without the letter for right

parts.note: Freud, founder of psychoanalysis; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist declares it wrong to argue.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, bitter dispute or quarrel between parties.

clue.text: Unity of chaps evident in a salute

indicators.note: the chaps are to be seen inside the following words

parts.note: to salute is to greet
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Comradeship among men shows in a salute.
explanation.definitionFit: Unity and accord both describe a state of being of one mind.

clue.text: Academic at ceremony may have this chicken

parts.words: Academic at ceremony may have this
parts.note: a graduate or don at a degree ceremony wears a mortarboard

explanation.surface: A scholar in academic dress at a graduation might be holding a chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated cockerel fattened for eating is a kind of chicken.

clue.text: Strong American coin no longer used

parts.note: solid means sturdy or strong

explanation.surface: A sturdy American coin has gone out of circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold piece of the late Roman Empire, long obsolete as currency.

clue.text: General flying in balloon

indicators.note: letters sent flying are scattered and land in a new order

explanation.surface: An army general is aloft in a hot-air balloon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like the officer and 'balloon' like the craft, but balloon is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To balloon is to swell or grow larger, the same as to make or become bigger.
